title.zh: 联邦庆典中的法国拱门

alt.en: A crowded procession passes beneath a decorated arch reading “France welcomes Australian Federation”; flags hang across the street.
alt.zh: 拥挤的游行队伍经过写有“法国欢迎澳大利亚联邦成立”的装饰拱门，街道上方悬挂旗帜。

caption.en: Sydney, 1901. A photograph of Federation celebrations beneath the French Arch, preserved as a film copy negative.
caption.zh: 悉尼，1901年。法国拱门下的联邦成立庆祝活动；馆藏为翻拍底片。

interpretation.en: The temporary arch and crowded street made Federation a public spectacle. The ceremony celebrated national unity while the founding arrangements excluded First Nations peoples.
interpretation.zh: 临时拱门与拥挤街道把联邦成立变成公共盛典。仪式庆祝国家团结，建国安排却仍排斥原住民。

title.en: A badge from the 1967 referendum campaign

alt.en: A round white badge bears black lettering: “VOTE YES FOR ABORIGINES”.
alt.zh: 白色圆形徽章上印有黑字：“VOTE YES FOR ABORIGINES”（为原住民投赞成票）。

caption.en: Campaign badge, about 1967. Modern collection photograph by Jon Augier, Museums Victoria. The inscription preserves the campaign’s historical wording.
caption.zh: 公投宣传徽章，约1967年。乔恩·奥吉尔为维多利亚博物馆拍摄的现代藏品照片。铭文保留当时宣传用语。

interpretation.en: A wearable slogan made support for constitutional reform visible in everyday life. Such campaign material accompanied years of Indigenous organizing and allied activism. The referendum changed constitutional provisions; it did not first confer citizenship or voting rights.
interpretation.zh: 可佩戴的口号使支持修宪的立场在日常生活中可见。这类宣传品伴随原住民及盟友多年的组织行动。公投改变了宪法条款，并非首次授予公民身份或投票权。
